caption: Also accepts a single list argument
A single argument is returned unchanged
The identity element folds into a normal call like any other argument
sage.note: compute-engine folds the inner Min() into its identity element +Infinity before combining with 5; Sage's inner min() has no identity for zero arguments and raises before the fold can happen.

caption: Nested lists are flattened into the pool
The numeric arguments collapse to their minimum; symbolic ones stay
The min of two [[Interval]]s is the interval of possible minima, $[-3, 3]$
The day's low from the same hourly readings. See [[Max]]
Infinities participate directly in the comparison rather than being filtered out
Multiple arguments -- lists included -- are flattened into one pool rather than compared list-by-list. See [[Max]]
With no arguments it returns the identity element $+\infty$ (Max, whose identity is $-\infty$, still returns NaN)
sage.note: compute-engine's Min() answers its identity element +Infinity, per Wolfram's convention; Sage's builtin min() has no identity for zero arguments and raises ValueError.

caption: The min of an empty list is NaN
sage.note: Both decline on an empty collection: compute-engine answers NaN for Min([]), and Sage's min() raises ValueError: min() iterable argument is empty.
sympy.note: compute-engine gives NaN for the min of an empty list; SymPy's Min() is the identity ∞.
